headline: Project NOAH Head Says Decades of Ignoring 1941 Flood Plan Worsened Flood Risk
seoTitle: Project NOAH Head on 1941 Flood Control Plan | FMB News
seoDescription: UP resilience expert Mahar Lagmay said decades of failure to follow a 1941 flood-control master plan contributed to recurring flooding.
deck: Mahar Lagmay called for science-based, system-wide flood planning rather than disconnected projects as severe flooding continued.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: UP Resilience Institute executive director and Project NOAH head Mahar Lagmay said recurring flooding reflects decades of failure to follow a comprehensive flood-control master plan drafted in 1941.
He argued that flood mitigation should be treated as a connected watershed and drainage problem rather than as a collection of isolated projects.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The comments came as Metro Manila and parts of Luzon experienced prolonged flooding after repeated monsoon rain.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Flood-control infrastructure can shift water problems downstream if projects are designed without basin-wide hydrology, land-use planning and drainage capacity in mind.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The policy question is whether national and local agencies will align future flood-control spending with updated science-based basin plans and transparent project evaluation.
